central_unknown: Can Ferrari's improved straight-line speed and battery management hold up at Spa's long straights, or will the longest lap on the calendar expose lingering power deployment weaknesses? Also, Spa's microclimate weather could introduce rain uncertainty that reshuffles the order.

budget_tiers.core: Antonelli (2x), Hadjar, Lindblad/Lawson, Hulkenberg/Bortoleto, Mercedes, Ferrari
budget_tiers.fills: Hulkenberg (price floor) or Bortoleto if budget allows; Colapinto as a stretch option

budget_tiers.core: Antonelli (2x), Lindblad, Lawson, Hulkenberg, Mercedes, Ferrari
budget_tiers.fills: Bortoleto over Hulkenberg if affordable; bank budget for final fix flexibility

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Mercedes expected to be strong at Spa (historical success, best car on grid). Antonelli has monopolized fastest lap points (3 of 4 sprints, majority of GPs), providing floor on bad weekends. After Hamilton was the Silverstone differential, consensus shifts back to Antonelli as the safe primary 2x for Belgium.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Lewis Hamilton
captains.reason: Hamilton showed strong form at Silverstone (sprint pole, P3 in GP). Ferrari's improved straight-line speed bodes well for Spa's long straights. Better budget increase thresholds than Antonelli. However, FormulaFantasyHub notes Antonelli owners are 'in the box seat this weekend,' making Hamilton the clear differential rather than primary pick.

buy.name: Isaac Hadjar
buy.note: Four or five consecutive top-6 finishes; has outqualified Verstappen three times this season. Strong budget builder with low thresholds (~-2 for min rise, ~10 for max). Consensus top B-tier pick across all channels.

buy.name: Arvid Lindblad
buy.note: Fourth consecutive double-points finish for VCARB. Excellent budget builder at rock-bottom price. Racing Bulls form as fifth-fastest team cements his value.

buy.name: Liam Lawson
buy.note: Consistent points finisher, averaging ~13 points in non-DNF races. VCARB's form is strong. Slightly harder budget thresholds than Lindblad but solid hold.

buy.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
buy.note: Strong 16-point haul at Silverstone. Budget thresholds very favorable (-3 for min, 3 for max). FormulaFantasyHub recommends him over Hulkenberg if budget allows.

consider.name: Franco Colapinto
consider.note: Best price-rise thresholds among B-tier drivers (-8 for 0.2 rise, 1 for 0.6 rise). F1FantasyPolePosition calls him a popular target. More expensive than alternatives but strong budget upside. Alpine's form has been trending down since Barcelona however.

consider.name: Nico Hulkenberg
consider.note: Price floor asset — cannot lose value. Audi reliability appears fixed. Had a DNF at Silverstone but still the cheapest enabler for premium builds. If he scores ~5 points, he'll be on for a price rise at Hungary.

consider.name: Esteban Ocon
consider.note: F1FantasyPolePosition notes he consistently gets minimum price rises. Consolation pick if 0.1M short of Colapinto. Not a priority target.

avoid: Valtteri Bottas — Three consecutive mechanical DNFs; Cadillac reliability a disaster. Wait until he finishes a race before considering.
Pierre Gasly — Alpine trending in wrong direction since Barcelona; replaced by Hadjar in most optimal builds.
Ollie Bearman — Haas drifting toward backmarker range rather than closing on midfield; likely another price drop.
Sergio Perez / Cadillac — Cadillac cars literally falling apart; DNF risk too high.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: Multiple sources (FanAmp, ZachGP) identified Silverstone as the last great Limitless opportunity. If you used it there, great. If not, Spa is less ideal because it's not a sprint weekend, reducing the points ceiling that makes Limitless worthwhile. Save for a future sprint weekend with clearer top-5 separation.

chips.name: 3x Boost (Extra DRS)
chips.reason: FanAmp specifically recommends saving for Zandvoort or Singapore where a 4A lineup becomes more viable and projected advantage over non-chip teams is larger. Without a sprint, the 3x multiplier at Spa won't generate enough edge (~40 points) to justify the chip.

chips.name: Autopilot
chips.reason: ZachGP notes more sprint races are coming with better B-tier options. Wait for a sprint weekend where the autopilot algorithm can capture both sprint and race points with a cleaner driver pool.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: If you're significantly behind on budget building and need to restructure (e.g., still carrying Bottas or missed the Hadjar/Lindblad wave), Belgium could be a reset point before the summer break. Otherwise, save.

watch_items: Ferrari straight-line speed at Spa: improved battery management and energy deployment seen at Silverstone needs to hold on F1's longest lap. Watch FP1/FP2 speed trap data through sectors 1 and 3.
Spa microclimate weather: 25% rain chance on Sunday. Mixed conditions could reshuffle the order and create DNF/overtake chaos — monitor forecasts closely before deadline.

VCARB (Racing Bulls) reliability: Four consecutive double-points finishes for both drivers. Any mechanical issue would hurt the most popular B-tier stack. Watch for signs of stress on the longest circuit.

Red Bull overnight improvements: FanAmp notes no team is better at finding pace overnight. Verstappen could jump into contention after Friday — keep budget for a potential final fix to Red Bull constructor.

Alpine's continued decline: Gasly and Colapinto have been trending down since Barcelona. If Alpine show life in practice, Colapinto becomes more attractive; if not, confirms the pivot to Racing Bulls B-tier stack.
Cadillac/Bottas reliability: Need to see a clean race finish before anyone considers bringing Bottas back, even at 3.0M price floor.
Pirelli going a step softer (C2/C3/C4) at Spa: Could introduce multi-stop strategies and more varied racing, potentially benefiting overtaking and midfield shuffles.
arc: Belgium is a transitional race before the summer break and the back-half sprint cluster. The consensus is to consolidate gains from Silverstone — lock in Antonelli as your 2x, secure the Racing Bulls B-tier trio (Hadjar/Lindblad/Lawson), and pair Mercedes with Ferrari as constructors. Budget building remains critical: Hadjar, Lindblad, and Bortoleto all have favorable thresholds. The 4A lineup strategy (four Tier-A level drivers) is not yet viable because B-tier options like Hulkenberg/Bottas don't reliably finish races, but it becomes a real possibility at Zandvoort or Singapore where sprint weekends and better B-tier reliability could unlock the 3x Boost or Extra DRS chips. Save your premium chips — Hungary and the late-season sprints at Zandvoort and Singapore are the targets. Use Belgium to bank budget, roll a transfer forward, and position for aggressive moves after the summer break.
